clean_source_blocks.text: The Houthis said the embargo was a response to a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Yemen Yemen's Houthis have announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia. The Iran-backed group's military spokesman said it would begin immediately and was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen. He gave few details about the embargo but a Houthi media official said they were closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the southern gateway to the Red Sea, to Saudi vessels. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. The Red Sea has become crucial for oil shipments from Saudi Arabia during the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf. Second tanker in three months hijacked off Yemen by suspected Somali pirates
The Houthis say the embargo begins immediately and is a response to a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Yemen.

DUBAI/CAIRO, July 20 - Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, a move that opens a new front against the United States in its war on Iran and widens the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf. Iran had pressed the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the U.S. continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure. In their statement, the Houthis’ armed forces said they were declaring “a maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of ‘an eye for an eye’, effective immediately...” They said the decision was in response to what they called “an unjust and oppressive siege” imposed on Yemen by the Saudis. There was no immediate response from Saudi Arabia.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN. On Monday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi Arabia had imposed an "unjust and oppressive siege on our dear people for nearly 12 years, plundering our resources and imposing a comprehensive blockade on our ports and airports by land, sea, and air".

DUBAI/CAIRO, July 20 - Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, a move that opens a new front against the United States in its war on Iran and widens the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf.

Iran had pressed the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the U.S. continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure.

In their statement, the Houthis’ armed forces said they were declaring “a maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of ‘an eye for an eye’, effective immediately...”

They said the decision was in response to what they called “an unjust and oppressive siege” imposed on Yemen by the Saudis.

There was no immediate response from Saudi Arabia.

The full closure of the Bab el-Mandeb strait would reduce global oil supply by 7% as it would leave most of Saudi oil exports unable to leave the region. The disruption would add to the massive cut to global oil flows from the war in the Gulf, which has already reduced shipments by 10% of global supply.

The Houthis’ announcement followed signs from both Iran and the U.S. that they wanted to resume diplomatic efforts to end an escalating cycle of attacks that has all but wrecked a fragile interim agreement signed last month.

A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Monday that Tehran had received a proposal from mediators for a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to salvage the interim deal, intended to pave the way to a lasting agreement to the war that began on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran.

Oil prices briefly jumped above $90 a barrel earlier on Monday after renewed disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. They later pared gains after Iran’s Foreign Ministry said mediators had recently presented proposals to Tehran, signaling that diplomatic contacts remain active.

Neither the ministry nor the official who spoke to Reuters gave any further details on the putative ceasefire discussions.

Separately, two Pakistani government sources said Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni, making his second visit to Islamabad in less than a week, had asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in Iran’s conflict with the United States.

The diplomatic flurry came after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had struck U.S. military assets across the region following another night of U.S. bombardment of Iranian cities.

payload.title: Jemenin huthit julistivat merisaarron Saudi-Arabiaa vastaan
payload.summary: Huthit ilmoittivat sulkevansa Bab al-Mandabin salmen Saudi-Arabian aluksilta. Välittömästi alkavaksi julistetun saarron käytännön toteutus jäi epäselväksi.
payload.content:
Jemenin Iranin tukemat huthit ilmoittivat maanantaina asettavansa Saudi-Arabian välittömään merisaartoon. Ryhmä perusteli päätöstä Saudi-Arabian Jemenille asettamalla saarrolla, joka sen mukaan rajoittaa satamia ja lentoasemia huthien hallitsemassa Luoteis-Jemenissä sekä maa-, meri- ja ilmayhteyksiä. Saudi-Arabian viranomaiset eivät olleet heti kommentoineet ilmoitusta, eikä huthien lausunto sisältänyt tarkkoja tietoja saarron käytännön toteutuksesta.

## Bab al-Mandab suljetaan saudialuksilta

Huthien mediaedustajan mukaan ryhmä aikoo sulkea Bab al-Mandabin salmen Saudi-Arabian aluksilta. Salmi on Punaisenmeren eteläinen portti, joten ilmoitus kohdistuu keskeiseen merireittiin. Huthien sotilaallinen tiedottaja Yahya Sarea kuvasi päätöstä ”silmä silmästä” -periaatteeseen perustuvaksi vastatoimeksi ja syytti Saudi-Arabiaa lähes 12 vuotta jatkuneesta epäoikeudenmukaisesta ja sortavasta saarrosta.

Ryhmä ilmoitti saarron alkavan välittömästi, mutta ei täsmentänyt, miten se aikoo valvoa liikennettä, mitä Saudi-Arabian aluksia päätös tarkalleen koskee tai millaisia toimia se suunnittelee niitä vastaan. Iran oli painostanut hutheja sulkemaan Bab al-Mandabin, jos Yhdysvallat jatkaisi iskujaan Iranin sähköinfrastruktuuriin. Päätös kytkeytyy näin myös Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin Irania vastaan käymään sotaan.

## Punaisenmeren merkitys öljykuljetuksille kasvoi

Punaisenmeren merkitys Saudi-Arabian öljykuljetuksille on kasvanut Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin Irania vastaan käymän sodan aikana. Syynä on se, että Hormuzinsalmi Persianlahdella on käytännössä sulkeutunut. Bab al-Mandabiin kohdistuva ilmoitus laajentaa siksi energiatoimituksiin ja kansainväliseen kauppaan kohdistuvaa uhkaa Persianlahden ulkopuolelle Punaisellemerelle, vaikka saarron todelliset vaikutukset eivät olleet vielä selvillä.

## Jemenin sota jatkunut vuodesta 2014

Jemenin sisällissota alkoi vuonna 2014, kun huthit syrjäyttivät maan hallituksen Sanaasta. Konflikti laajeni seuraavana vuonna, kun Saudi-Arabian johtama arabimaiden liittouma puuttui sotaan yrittäessään palauttaa hallituksen valtaan. Huthit ovat sittemmin hallinneet Luoteis-Jemeniä. Juuri tämän alueen satamiin ja lentoasemiin kohdistuvaa saartoa ryhmä käyttää nyt perusteena Saudi-Arabian vastaiselle toimelleen.

Taisteluissa on tiettävästi kuollut yli 150 000 ihmistä, ja sota on synnyttänyt yhden maailman vakavimmista humanitaarisista kriiseistä. YK:n mukaan yli 22 miljoonaa ihmistä tarvitsee jonkinlaista apua. Sarea väitti Saudi-Arabian myös ryöstäneen Jemenin luonnonvaroja pitkän saarron aikana. Humanitaarinen tilanne muodostaa taustan huthien väitteelle, jonka mukaan Saudi-Arabia on rajoittanut Jemenin yhteyksiä lähes 12 vuoden ajan. Koska huthit eivät kertoneet toimeenpanon keinoista, ilmoituksen vaikutukset Bab al-Mandabin laivaliikenteeseen jäivät maanantaina avoimiksi.
summary_bullets: Huthit julistivat Saudi-Arabiaa vastaan välittömästi alkavan merisaarron.
Ryhmän mukaan Bab al-Mandabin salmi suljetaan Saudi-Arabian aluksilta.
Saudi-Arabia ei ollut kommentoinut ilmoitusta, ja saarron toteutustapa jäi avoimeksi.
payload.journalist_note: Saarron käytännön laajuus ja toteutustapa jäivät avoimiksi, eikä Saudi-Arabian kommenttia ollut saatavilla.

Juuri tämän alueen satamiin ja lentoasemiin kohdistuvaa saartoa ryhmä käyttää nyt perusteena Saudi-Arabian vastaiselle toimelleen.

Taisteluissa on tiettävästi kuollut yli 150 000 ihmistä, ja sota on synnyttänyt yhden maailman vakavimmista humanitaarisista kriiseistä. YK:n mukaan yli 22 miljoonaa ihmistä tarvitsee jonkinlaista apua. Sarea väitti Saudi-Arabian myös ryöstäneen Jemenin luonnonvaroja pitkän saarron aikana. Humanitaarinen tilanne muodostaa taustan huthien väitteelle, jonka mukaan Saudi-Arabia on rajoittanut Jemenin yhteyksiä lähes 12 vuoden ajan. Koska huthit eivät kertoneet toimeenpanon keinoista, ilmoituksen vaikutukset Bab al-Mandabin laivaliikenteeseen jäivät maanantaina avoimiksi.

The Iran-backed group's military spokesman said it would begin immediately and was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen. He gave few details about the embargo but a Houthi media official said they were closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the southern gateway to the Red Sea, to Saudi vessels. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. DUBAI/CAIRO, July 20 - Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they were imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, a move that opens a new front against the United States in its war on Iran and widens the threat to global energy supplies and trade beyond the Gulf. Iran had pressed the Houthis to close the Bab el-Mandeb gateway to the Red Sea if the U.S. continued to attack Iranian power infrastructure. In their statement, the Houthis’ armed forces said they were declaring “a maritime embargo against the criminal Saudi enemy, based on the equation of ‘an eye for an eye’, effective immediately...” They said the decision was in response to what they called “an unjust and oppressive siege” imposed on Yemen by the Saudis. There was no immediate response from Saudi Arabia.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN. On Monday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said Saudi Arabia had imposed an "unjust and oppressive siege on our dear people for nearly 12 years, plundering our resources and imposing a comprehensive blockade on our ports and airports by land, sea, and air".
